questions.question: The length of the common chord of two circles of radii 15 cm and 13 cm, whose centres are 14 cm apart, is:

Concept Used:

AM² = PA² - PM²

⇒ AM2 = 152 - PM2

⇒ AM2 = 225 - PM2 -----(1)

In ΔAMQ, QA = 13 cm

By Pythagoras theorem,

AM2 = QA2 - MQ2

⇒ AM2 = 132 - MQ2

⇒ AM2 = 169 - MQ2 -----(2)

From (1) and (2)

225 - PM2 = 169 - MQ2 

⇒ PM2 - MQ2 = 56

⇒ (PM + MQ) (PM - MQ) = 56

According to the question,

(PM + MQ) = PQ = Distance between centres = 14 cm ----(3)

⇒ (PM - MQ) = 56/14 = 4 ----(4)

From (3) and (4)

PM = 9 cm

Putting value of PM in (1)

AM2 = 225 - 92

⇒ AM2 = 225 - 81

⇒ AM2 = 144

⇒ AM = 12 cm

Thus, length of common chord = AB = 2AM = 24 cm

**∴ The length of the common chord is 24 cm.**

questions.question: In a mixture, milk and water are in ratio of 2 : 3. Some milk is added to the mixture because of which ratio of milk and water becomes 10 : 3. How much milk was added as a percentage of initial mixture?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial ratio of milk and water = 2:3

Final ratio of milk and water = 10:3

**Concept:**

We need to find the initial quantities of milk and water and then determine the amount of milk added to achieve the new ratio. Finally, we calculate the added milk as a percentage of the initial mixture.

**Calculation:**

Let the initial quantities of milk and water be 2x and 3x respectively.

In the final mixture, let the quantity of milk be 2x + M and the quantity of water be 3x.

Given final ratio: (2x + M) / 3x = 10 / 3

⇒ 3(2x + M) = 10 × 3x

⇒ 6x + 3M = 30x

⇒ 3M = 24x

⇒ M = 8x

Initial mixture = 2x + 3x = 5x

Milk added as a percentage of initial mixture:

⇒ (M / (5x)) × 100%

⇒ (8x / (5x)) × 100%

⇒ (8 / 5) × 100%

⇒ 1.6 × 100%

⇒ 160%

**∴ The correct answer is option 3, 160%.**

questions.question: A car can cover 275 km in 5 hours. If its speed is reduced by 5 km/h, then how much time will the car take to cover a distance of 250 km?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered by the car = 275 km

Time taken = 5 hours

Speed of the car = Distance / Time = 275 km / 5 hr = 55 km/h

New speed of the car = 55 km/h - 5 km/h = 50 km/h

Distance to be covered = 250 km

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

New time taken to cover 250 km at 50 km/h

⇒ Time = 250 km / 50 km/h

⇒ Time = 5 hours

**∴ The car will take 5 hours to cover 250 km.**

questions.question: Walking at (5)/(7) of his normal speed, Manish is 20 minutes late in reaching. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and office is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Let the usual time taken by Manish to cover the distance be t minutes.

Manish walks at 5/7 of his normal speed and is 20 minutes late.

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Difference in time = Normal time - Late time

**Calculations:**

Let the normal speed be S and the normal time be t.

Distance = Speed × Time = S × t

When walking at 5/7 of his normal speed, the speed becomes (5/7) × S.

The time taken to cover the same distance at this speed is:

New time = (S × t) ÷ (5/7 × S) = (7 × t) ÷ 5

So, the difference in time is:

Difference = New time - Normal time = (7 × t) ÷ 5 - t

Given, the difference in time is 20 minutes:

(7t ÷ 5) - t = 20

⇒ (7t ÷ 5) - (5t ÷ 5) = 20

⇒ 2t ÷ 5 = 20

⇒ t = 20 × 5 / 2 = 50 minutes

**∴ The usual time taken by Manish to cover the distance is 50 minutes.**

questions.question: In a equilateral triangle ΔABC, the interior angle bisector for ∠B and exterior angle bisector for ∠C meets at E. Find the ∠BEC.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The angle formed by the intersection of an interior angle bisector of one vertex and the exterior angle bisector of another vertex is always half of the third angle of the triangle.

Formula: ∠BEC = (1/2) × ∠A

Since ΔABC is an equilateral triangle, all interior angles are 60°.

∴ ∠A = 60°

∠BEC = 60° ÷ 2 = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ΔABC is equilateral, ∠B interior bisector and ∠C exterior bisector meet at E.

**Formula Used:** Interior angles of equilateral triangle = 60°; Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8003f07d4fd16b4bd885f9f3aab8d7db7dd0ea4a4614655276fa671a8d411a52.png] 

⇒ In equilateral ΔABC, ∠ABC = ∠BCA = ∠BAC = 60°.

⇒ ∠EBC is the interior bisector of ∠ABC ⇒ ∠EBC = 60° ÷ 2 = 30°.

⇒ Exterior ∠ACD = 180° − ∠BCA = 180° − 60° = 120°.

⇒ ∠ACE is the exterior bisector of ∠ACD ⇒ ∠ACE = 120° ÷ 2 = 60°.

⇒ ∠BCE = ∠BCA + ∠ACE = 60° + 60° = 120°.

⇒ In ΔBCE, ∠EBC + ∠BCE + ∠BEC = 180°.

⇒ 30° + 120° + ∠BEC = 180°.

⇒ ∠BEC = 180° − 150° = 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Incenter Properties

The intersection of all three interior angle bisectors is the incenter. The angle formed at the incenter I is ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A/2.

Excenter Properties

The intersection of two exterior angle bisectors is the excenter. The angle formed at the excenter E is ∠BEC = 90° − ∠A/2.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. ∠ACD = ∠BAC + ∠ABC.</p

questions.question: The price of 1 kg of grapes is increased by 5 percent and the nominal increase is by Rs. 10. What is the new price of the grapes per kg?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The price of 1 kg of grapes is increased by 5%, and the nominal increase is ₹10.

**Formula used:**

Nominal Increase = Original Price × (Percentage Increase / 100)

New Price = Original Price + Nominal Increase

**Calculation:**

Let the original price of 1 kg of grapes = ₹x.

Nominal Increase = ₹10

⇒ 10 = x × (5/100)

⇒ x = 10 × (100/5) = ₹200

New Price = Original Price + Nominal Increase

⇒ New Price = ₹200 + ₹10 = ₹210

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A and B together can finish a job in 20 days. B and C together can finish the same job in 30 days. If A and C together can finish it in 24 days, in how many days can A alone finish the job?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B = 20 days

B and C = 30 days

A and C = 24 days

**Formula used:**

Total work = LCM of days

Efficiency = Total work / Days

**Calculation:**

LCM of 20, 30, and 24 = 120 units

Efficiency of A and B = 120 / 20 = 6 units/day

Efficiency of B and C = 120 / 30 = 4 units/day

Efficiency of A and C = 120 / 24 = 5 units/day

Adding all efficiencies:

(A + B) + (B + C) + (A + C) = 6 + 4 + 5

2(A + B + C) = 15

A + B + C = 15 / 2 = 7.5 units/day

Efficiency of A = (A + B + C) - (B + C)

Efficiency of A = 7.5 - 4 = 3.5 units/day

Days taken by A alone = Total work / Efficiency of A

Days taken by A alone = 120 / 3.5

Days taken by A alone = 1200 / 35

Days taken by A alone = 240 / 7

Days taken by A alone = 34 ²/₇ days

**∴ A alone can finish the job in 34 ²/₇ days.**

questions.question: The average of 13 numbers is 22. If each number is multiplied by 3, what will be the new average?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If each number in a given set is multiplied by a certain constant, the new average is simply the old average multiplied by the same constant.

New Average = Old Average × Constant

New Average = 22 × 3 = 66

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of 13 numbers = 22

Constant multiplier for each number = 3

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 Property of Averages
 
 Original Average:
 
 22
 
 
• 
 

 Each number × 3
 
 New Average:
 
 66 (i.e. 22 × 3)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of the original 13 numbers = Average × Total numbers

⇒ Original Sum = 22 × 13 = 286

⇒ When each individual number is multiplied by 3, the total sum is also multiplied by 3.

⇒ New Sum = Original Sum × 3

⇒ New Sum = 286 × 3 = 858

⇒ New Average = New Sum ÷ Total numbers

⇒ New Average = 858 ÷ 13 = 66

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Addition and Subtraction Property

If a constant value 'k' is added to or subtracted from each observation in a dataset, the new average becomes (Old Average + k) or (Old Average − k).

Multiplication and Division Property

If each observation is multiplied or divided by a non-zero constant 'k', the new average becomes (Old Average × k) or (Old Average ÷ k).

Combined Average

If group 1 has n₁ items with average A₁ and group 2 has n₂ items with average A₂, the Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: The value of cosec 30° − cos 60° is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly substitute standard trigonometric values from the table.

cosec 30° = 2

cos 60° = 1/2

Calculation: 2 − 1/2 = 3/2

**∴ The correct answer is 3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Expression: cosec 30° − cos 60°

Formula used: Standard values of trigonometric ratios.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/735b3eb7bba87cd80fd8ff5b96896d5dd2561ec0619a57d19d1bc545fc9a2032.png] 

⇒ cosec 30° = 1 ÷ sin 30°

⇒ Since sin 30° = 1/2, then cosec 30° = 1 ÷ (1/2) = 2

⇒ From the standard table, cos 60° = 1/2

⇒ Substitute these values into the expression:

⇒ 2 − 1/2

⇒ (4 − 1) ÷ 2

⇒ 3/2

**∴ The correct answer is 3/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Reciprocal Identities

Trigonometric functions have reciprocal pairs: cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Complementary Angles

For any angle θ, sin θ = cos(90° − θ). Thus, sin 30° = cos(90° − 30°) = cos 60° = 1/2.

Standard Trigonometric Values

Important values to remember: sin 0°=0, sin 30°=1/2, sin 45°=1/√2, sin 60°=√3/2, sin 90°=1.</p

Therefore, the expression becomes (4 × 281 × 119) ÷ (281 × 119) = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: a = 281, b = 119

Method: Expansion of algebraic identities

⇒ Given Expression = ((281 + 119)² − (281 − 119)²) ÷ (281 × 119)

⇒ Let a = 281 and b = 119, then the expression is ((a + b)² − (a − b)²) ÷ (ab)

⇒ Expanding (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

⇒ Expanding (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

⇒ Numerator = (a² + b² + 2ab) − (a² + b² − 2ab) = 4ab

⇒ Expression = 4ab ÷ ab = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Identity

The sum of the square of the sum and the square of the difference is given by: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²).

Difference of Squares

The formula a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) is frequently used in simplification to factorize quadratic terms.

BODMAS Rule

Always follow the Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction order for multi-step calculations.</p

questions.question: The radius of a 80 cm wide road roller is 77 cm. Find the number of revolutions that the roller will take to cover an area of 96.8 m². [Take π = (22)/(7)]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radius of an 80 cm wide road roller is 77 cm.

The roller covers an area of 96.8 m².

**Formula used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cylinder = 2πrh

where, r = radius of cylinder

h = height of cylinder

No. of revolutions = Total area / CSA

**Calculation:**

Radius of road roller = 77 cm = 0.77 m

Height of road roller = 80 cm = 0.8 m

The curved surface area of the roller 

CSA = 2 × π × (0.77) × (0.8)

⇒ CSA = 2 × ((22)/(7)) × (0.616)

⇒ CSA = ((1.232 × 22))/(7)

⇒ CSA = (27.104)/(7) = 3.872 m²

The roller will take to cover an area of 96.8 m².

No. of revolutions = (96.8)/(3.872) = 25 revolutions,

**∴ The number of revolutions that the roller will take is 25.**

questions.question: If Vivek got 70% marks in 6 papers of 100 marks each, where 15% of total marks he scored in physics. How many number does he scored in physics.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total papers = 6

Marks per paper = 100

Percentage scored = 70%

Percentage of marks scored in Physics = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Total Marks Scored = Percentage Scored × Total Marks

Marks in Physics = Percentage of Marks in Physics × Total Marks Scored

**Calculation:**

Total Marks = 6 × 100 = 600

Total Marks Scored = 70% of 600

⇒ Total Marks Scored = (70/100) × 600

⇒ Total Marks Scored = 420

Marks in Physics = 15% of 420

⇒ Marks in Physics = (15/100) × 420

⇒ Marks in Physics = 63

**Vivek scored 63 marks in Physics.**

questions.question:
The length of the chord of a circle is 24 cm. The diameter of the circle is 40 cm. Find the distance of the chord from the center of the circle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d222e444265f1a5f0cbe5897d68966edbe0d036baa540d0d84ea60cde7e7989a.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The length of the cord = 24 cm

The diameter of the circle = 40 cm

The radius of the circle = 20 cm

**Formula Use:**

(Hypotenuse)² = (Base)² + (Perpendicular)²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40d3ac9bcbc72cc14d82e1799a77638d9b2018eb50fd3c25693b536bf9238812.png] 

Consider the △OAD,

Here, AO = Radius = 20 cm

AD = 12 cm

Therefore, According to the Pythagorus theorem,

(Hypotenuse)2 = (Base)2 + (Perpendicular)2

⇒ (AO)² = (AD)² + (OD)²

⇒ (20)² = (12)² + (OD)²

⇒ (OD)2 = 400 - 144

⇒ (OD)2 = 256

⇒ OD = sqrt 256

⇒ OD = 16 cm

**∴ The distance of the chord from the center of the circle is 16 cm.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Distance of the chord from the center (OD) = sqrt{r² - ({xover2})²}

⇒ sqrt{20² - ({24over2})²}

⇒ sqrt{400 - 144} = sqrt{256} = 16 cm

∴ The distance of the chord from the center of the circle is 16 cm.

questions.question: How much simple interest will Rs. 6,000 earn in 15 months at the rate of 12% per annum?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 6,000

Time (T) = 15 months = 15/12 years = 1.25 years

Rate (R) = 12% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

**Calculation:**

SI = (6000 × 12 × 1.25) / 100

⇒ SI = (6000 × 12 × 5) / (100 × 4)

⇒ SI = (72000 × 5) / 400

⇒ SI = 360000 / 400

⇒ SI = Rs. 900

**The simple interest earned is Rs. 900.**

questions.question: What sum would amount to 24520 in three year at 12% p. a rate of compound interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amount = Rs. 24520

Time period = 3 years

Rate of interest = 12%

**Formula Used:**

Amount = P( 1 + r/100 )ⁿ

Where, P = Principal

r = Rate of interest

n = Time period

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

Amount = P( 1 + r/100 )ⁿ

⇒ 24520 = P (1 + 12/100)³

⇒ 24520 = P (1 + 0.12)³

⇒ P = 24520/(1.12)³

⇒ P = 17452.85

**∴ The Principal is Rs. 17452.85.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**Compound Interest means interest earned on interest.

Simple interest always occurs on only principal but compound interest also occurs on simple interest. So, if time period is 2 years, compound interest will also apply on simple interest of first year.

questions.question: Two parallel chords on the same side of the centre of a circle are 12 cm and 20 cm long and the radius of the circle is 5√13 cm. What is the distance between the chords?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the first chord = 12 cm

Length of the second chord = 20 cm

Radius of the circle = 5√13 cm

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ed431c5f2b7efda01a6fa2fce18cf2e435451f2093ff8beca5645f5292c8d29.png] 

OB = OD = 5 √13 cm

AB = 12 cm, CD = 20 cm, AM = MB = 12/2 = 6 cm and CN = ND = 20/2 = 10 cm

In Δ MBO

OB2 = MB2 + MO2

⇒ (5 √13)2 = 62 + OM2

⇒ OM2 = 325 – 36 = 289

⇒ OM = √289 = 17

In Δ NDO

OD2 = ND2 + NO2

⇒ (5 √13)2 = 102 + NO2

⇒ ON2 = 325 – 100 = 225

ON = √225 = 15

As we know,

OM = MN + ON

⇒ 17 = MN + 15

⇒ MN = 17 – 15 = 2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**
